text: claude-sonnet-5-5 cost $0.1533, above the $0.1358 authorized for claude-sonnet-5-5

I'm not blocking this design. All three attacks went unconfirmed, and no check in the report fails.

Each attack returned the same numbers as the baseline report. The patch may not have changed the evaluated design, but I can't tell that from here. I treat the design as unproven under heavier-mass and low-efficiency conditions, not as shown to be robust.

Non-blocking concerns (no check measures these, or the margins are thin):
- Payload: payload_kg is 0. IREC 10k entries normally expect a payload of about 4 kg, and no check measures this. A real payload would add mass and push the vehicle toward the thin margins below.
- Apogee spread: the dispersion band is 2700-3450 m (about 8860-11,320 ft), and the nominal is already 0.8% high. A low-thrust, high-drag, windy flight would land about 11% under the contract altitude. The 5% accuracy check applies only to the nominal case.
- Injector stiffness: dP/Pc is 20% against a 15% minimum. Lower c* efficiency (below the default 0.90 the design assumes), orifice tolerances or feed losses erode this margin first. Low stiffness invites chamber-coupled instability.
- Tank margins: the tank proof margin is +0.231 (bulkhead stress 224 MPa against 276 MPa yield). The 14 mm bulkheads and 3.175 mm walls are thin, with MEOP at 44 bar. A weld, thread or wall-thickness shortfall could consume that margin.
- Stability: static margin at rail exit is 1.75 cal, only 0.25 cal above the 1.5 cal limit. The design has no weighed dry mass (measured_dry is null), so all mass and CG values are estimates until the vehicle is built and weighed.
- Igniter timing: the igniter burns 4.0 s, the main burn is 2.69 s, and start-sequence margin is +2.06 s. A slow valve, a longer feed-line fill or cold LOX would eat into it.
- Agent-chosen inputs: the agents picked LOX, ethanol and the $15,000 budget themselves. The BOM is $6,456, which leaves a lot of slack. No check measures LOX handling, cryogenic ground support or engine test plans, and the team still needs to do that work.
- Burn time: the 2.69 s burn leaves little time to catch an anomaly.

No blocking issue found. All 23 checks pass, and none of my five attacks were confirmed. Those attacks varied as-built dry mass, as-built CG, and test-stand c* efficiency (0.75, 0.80, 0.85). The host returned identical check values each time. That suggests these inputs don't propagate into the check run, or the design is effectively pinned. I read it as a gap in what was tested, not as proof the design is robust. I've used my attack budget and am finishing here.

Non-blocking concerns:
1. Tank margins are thin. tank_proof is +0.231 (bulkhead stress 224 MPa against 276 MPa yield) and tank_burst is +0.498. The tanks are 6061 with a 3.2 mm wall and 14 mm bulkheads. A weld or thread knockdown, or a hot-day MEOP rise, would erode this quickly.
2. Apogee accuracy only holds at nominal. The nominal apogee is 3071 m against a 3048 m contract, so the 5% band is about ±152 m. The design's own dispersion table runs from 2700 m to 3450 m, and several cases fall outside the band.
3. Injector stiffness is 20% against a 15% limit at Pc 29.9 bar. A c* shortfall that lowers Pc would erode this margin.
4. Rail exit speed is 111 ft/s against a 100 ft/s limit in the worst wind. That is only about 3.4 m/s of margin. Any extra mass or thrust loss comes straight out of it.
5. The agents assumed the oxidizer (LOX), the fuel (ethanol) and the $15,000 budget, because the request never stated them. The BOM is only $6,456. The team should confirm that LOX handling is practical for them.
6. The c* efficiency of 0.90 is the default, not a measured value. I'd want a real hot-fire to validate it. No check measures this.
7. The 2.69 s burn at about 3.5 kN is a short, fast flight. Max-Q is at 388 m and Mach is 0.88. Drift at apogee is 778 m, so recovery planning should allow for it.

I could not block this design. The report shows 0 of 23 checks failing, and all three of my attacks went unconfirmed. Those were a 29 kg as-built dry mass, a 27 kg mass with the CG moved aft, and a test-stand c* efficiency of 0.80.

Non-blocking concerns, none of which a check measures:
- Each unconfirmed attack returned the unchanged baseline report (apogee_accuracy +0.042, stability_min +0.249). That suggests the host may not have applied measured_dry or eta_cstar to the simulated vehicle. If so, the design has not been shown to hold up under as-built mass or efficiency.
- Apogee is dispersion-sensitive. The band across the nine dispersion cases is 2700 to 3450 m, against a 3048 m contract. That is roughly -11% to +13%, so the nominal 5% accuracy margin says little about the real flight.
- The static-margin floor is thin. The minimum margin is 1.75 cal against a 1.5 cal limit. Peak acceleration of 12.3 g is also fairly close to the 15 g cap.
- The assumptions the agents added (LOX, ethanol and the $15k budget) were not tested. The team must have LOX handling and a supplier.
- Several margins are thin. Injector dP/Pc is 20% against a 15% limit, and the tank_proof margin is small. The tank wall is 3.2 mm of 6061 and the bulkheads are 14 mm.
- The ablative liner has little reserve: 1.4 mm of char in a 3.0 mm chamber liner.
- The burn is only 2.69 s with a 4.0 s igniter. The igniter is still burning 2.05 s after LOX arrives, so the start sequence works, but there is no margin for a hard start or a late valve.
- The vehicle is built from off-the-shelf BOM parts. Parts that go out of stock would change the geometry and mass, and I did not test that.

The verdict action was not available in this session, so this summary is my final review.

Verdict: no blocking finding. I used all three attacks and the host confirmed none of them. The report shows 23 of 23 checks passing, so I have nothing to cite.

All three attacks changed `measured_dry` (heavier, aft CG, lighter). The results came back identical to the baseline (apogee margin +0.042, stability +0.249 cal). The host probably ignored `measured_dry` because it is a field of the person's own spec. Whatever the cause, the design has not been tested against a heavier or CG-shifted as-built vehicle.

Non-blocking concerns that no check measures, or that pass with thin margin:
1. Apogee spread. Nominal apogee is 3071 m (10077 ft), inside the 5% band. The dispersion table spans 2700 to 3450 m (about 8860 to 11320 ft), so the +5% thrust / -10% drag case overshoots by about 13%. The 5% accuracy check covers only the nominal case, and its margin is just +0.042. Real mass growth would eat that margin.
2. Tank margins. Tank burst margin is +0.498 and proof margin is +0.231 (bulkhead 224 MPa against a yield of 276 MPa). The walls are 3.2 mm of 6061 with 14 mm bulkheads at 44 bar MEOP. The check does not cover weld or joint quality, or LOX cold-soak effects. A hydrostatic proof test is needed before filling with LOX.
3. Rail exit speed is 33.8 m/s (111 ft/s) against a 100 ft/s limit, a margin of only 3.4 m/s. A heavier build or a lossy injector at low eta_cstar would erode it quickly.
4. Injector stiffness. dP/Pc is 20% against a 15% limit. Hole-tolerance or discharge-coefficient error could push it toward chugging, which no check measures.
5. Stability. Static margin is 1.75 cal at rail exit against a 1.5 cal minimum, a margin of only 0.25 cal. It was not tested against an aft dry-CG shift.
6. Assumed inputs. The agents chose the LOX/ethanol pairing and the $15,000 budget themselves. The BOM is $6456 and has not been stress-tested against price changes. LOX handling and cryogenic valve availability are outside the checks.
7. Thermal margin. The ablative liner is thin: char reaches 1.4 mm of a 3.0 mm liner in the chamber. This is fine for a 2.7 s burn but leaves no room for a longer one.
8. Parachute descent. The drogue band margin is +7.6 m/s and the main descent is 9.3 m/s. These are reasonable but depend on a 27 kg as-flown mass.
